note_sections.t: Clinical reassessment is required due to a confirmed prior biopsy and a continuing upward PSA trend.

First noted for an elevated PSA reading in 2022, this patient has since been managed within the outpatient setting. At fifty-two years of age, he works as a retired shopkeeper, lives with his wife in an assisted-living residence, and navigates daily life using a mobility frame. Moderate lower urinary tract symptoms yield an IPSS score of 16, yet he sustains a rigorous cycling regimen of roughly 30 kilometres three times weekly and restricts alcohol intake to five units per week. His medical background includes hypertension, Obesity (BMI >30), and osteoarthritis, managed with amlodipine, lisinopril, and paracetamol taken as needed. He remains a Current smoker (45 pack-yr). A recent routine surveillance colonoscopy returned normal results, and he reports no fresh pelvic pain or haematuria. A prior systematic biopsy identified low-volume disease, and his PSA continues to climb.

DRE: The prostate presents as symmetrically enlarged with a smooth, firm texture, lacking any palpable nodules or asymmetry. Vital signs remain stable, recording a blood pressure of 134/69 mmHg and a heart rate of 75 bpm. General observation shows a well-nourished individual walking with a standard mobility frame, exhibiting no acute distress or peripheral swelling.

admin: Mobility limitation (frame); ground-floor consult room preferred.
